clue.text: Split tongue, perhaps

parts.note: Split is a Croatian port city, so the language spoken there is a tongue of the former Yugoslavia, not a forked tongue

explanation.surface: A forked tongue, like a snake's, is offered as an example.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Split' looks like a verb or adjective meaning forked; it is the city on Croatia's Adriatic coast.
explanation.definitionFit: The language of Croatia and Serbia is spoken in the city of Split, so it is that city's tongue.

clue.text: Mythical princess, universal in comic opera

indicators.note: in means the universal letter goes inside the jumbled word
comic suggests something absurd and mixed up, so opera is rearranged

parts.note: U is the film classification for universal viewing

explanation.surface: A legendary princess appears in a light-hearted opera suitable for all.
explanation.definitionFit: In Greek myth, the Phoenician princess carried off by Zeus disguised as a bull.

clue.text: About five, porter has time for a drink

indicators.note: about means surrounding, so the porter word goes round the five

parts.note: porter is a dark beer
V is the Roman numeral for five
an age is a period of time

explanation.surface: Around five o'clock a hotel porter takes time off for a drink.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Porter' looks like a hotel worker; it is the dark beer.
explanation.definitionFit: Any drinkable liquid, such as tea or juice, is a beverage.

clue.text: This casting can transform sad picture

indicators.note: can transform means the letters of sad picture may be changed into a new arrangement

explanation.surface: A gloomy image could be brightened by a slapstick throw.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Casting' looks like choosing actors; it means throwing, a slapstick missile.
explanation.definitionFit: A pie of cream or custard is thrown in the face in slapstick comedy, so it is something cast.

clue.text: Eminence in Greece is heaven for poets

explanation.surface: A Greek peak is described as paradise for poets.
explanation.definitionFit: A mountain in northern Greece is a high eminence; in poetry it is the home of the gods, a heaven.

clue.text: The raspberries unusually good from first signs — get a basket

indicators.note: first signs means the opening letter of each of these words is taken

explanation.surface: Unusually good raspberries prompt a gardener to fetch a basket.
explanation.walkthrough: A TRUG is a shallow wooden basket used by British gardeners.
explanation.definitionFit: A shallow oblong garden container of wooden strips for carrying produce or flowers.

clue.text: Flat delivery on even pitch

explanation.surface: A dull speech delivered without variation.
explanation.definitionFit: A speech given without any rise and fall is flat; a single unvarying pitch describes it.

clue.text: Behind gets a smack — you'll be aware of it later!

definitions.text: you'll be aware of it later!

parts.note: behind means after, later in sequence
a smack is a taste or flavour, as in 'a smack of garlic'

explanation.surface: Someone is spanked on the backside and will feel it later.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Behind' and 'smack' suggest a spanking; they mean after and flavour.
explanation.definitionFit: A flavour lingering in the mouth after eating is noticed only later.

clue.text: Jazz figure admits post office fraud

indicators.note: admits means one piece lets the other in, so the jazz figure holds the post office

parts.note: a riff is a repeated phrase in jazz

explanation.surface: A jazz musician is caught in a post office swindle.
explanation.definitionFit: A swindle in which someone is overcharged is a fraud on them.

clue.text: Effort to conceal a waistcoat in drag act

indicators.note: to conceal means the effort word wraps round and hides the other pieces

parts.note: an effort is a try
vest is the American word for a waistcoat

explanation.surface: A performer tries to hide a waistcoat during a cross-dressing show.
explanation.walkthrough: VEST for waistcoat is American usage; in Britain a vest is an undershirt.
explanation.definitionFit: Travesty originally meant dressing in another's clothes, a burlesque disguise, hence a cross-dressing performance.

clue.text: Big-footed creature, to let out the clutch on a hill

definitions.text: Big-footed creature, to let out the clutch on a hill

parts.words: Big-footed creature, to let out the clutch on a hill
parts.note: the name literally means big foot, and these Australasian birds hatch their clutch of eggs in a mound of earth, not by a car driver releasing a clutch pedal on a slope

explanation.surface: A driving lesson: easing out the clutch while stopped on a slope.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Clutch' and 'hill' paint a hill start in a car; the clutch is a set of eggs and the hill the mound these birds build to incubate them.
explanation.definitionFit: Mound-building birds of Australasia with large feet leave their eggs to incubate in heaps of rotting vegetation.

clue.text: Pygmalion's sculpture appears without leaf for festive occasion

indicators.note: without means the leaf word is taken away from the sculpture's name

parts.note: in Greek myth Pygmalion carved a statue later named Galatea, which came to life
tea is a dried leaf, as in loose-leaf tea

explanation.surface: A famous statue is shown without a fig leaf at a celebration.
explanation.definitionFit: A gala is a festive public event or celebration.

clue.text: Hebdomadal drinker breaking ageing laws

indicators.note: breaking means the letters of ageing laws are broken up and rearranged

explanation.surface: A weekly drinker flouts licensing laws as they get older.
explanation.walkthrough: Hebdomadal means weekly: a glass weekly, punning on the Glasgow native.
explanation.definitionFit: A native of Glasgow, punned as someone taking a glass weekly.

clue.text: Meandering in Rhode Island, you say?

explanation.surface: Someone asks whether a winding route is in a small US state.
explanation.walkthrough: Spoken, 'Rhode Island' is 'road island': a traffic island in the road, which is what a British roundabout is.
explanation.definitionFit: A circuitous, indirect route meanders; a road island at a junction is a traffic circle.

clue.text: Car, concave on the outside, has depreciated

indicators.note: on the outside means the concave word wraps round the car

parts.note: dished means hollowed, concave
the Mini is a small British car

explanation.surface: A car with a dented body has lost value.
explanation.definitionFit: Something that has lost value or size has been reduced.

clue.text: Shot at test

parts.note: to tempt someone is to test their resolve

explanation.surface: Someone takes a shot at an exam.
explanation.definitionFit: Having a shot at something means trying it, making an effort.

clue.text: Opening that lets down many an actor

definitions.text: Opening that lets down many an actor

parts.words: Opening that lets down many an actor
parts.note: suggests a first night that disappoints the cast, but means a hatch in a stage floor that drops actors below

explanation.surface: A first night that disappoints many performers.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Opening' reads as a premiere and 'lets down' as disappoints; it is a hinged hole in the stage.
explanation.definitionFit: A hinged panel in a stage floor lowers performers out of sight.

clue.text: Having to strike. I am approaching the newspapers

indicators.note: approaching means coming right up to, so the first piece sits immediately before the second

parts.note: I am contracts to I'm
the press is the collective name for newspapers

explanation.surface: Someone about to go on strike is talking to the papers.
explanation.definitionFit: To strike someone is to make an impression on them, as in 'it struck me as odd'.

clue.text: Limit holiday with bad weather

parts.note: a holiday is a rest
rain is bad weather

explanation.surface: A rainy holiday is a restricted one.
explanation.definitionFit: To hold back or curb something is to limit it.

clue.text: Beethoven concerto not covered in the Andersen recital

definitions.text: not covered in the Andersen recital

explanation.surface: A Beethoven piano concerto is played at a reading of fairy tales.
explanation.walkthrough: Beethoven's fifth piano concerto has this nickname; in Hans Christian Andersen's tale a ruler parades naked in his 'new clothes'.
explanation.definitionFit: Beethoven's fifth piano concerto bears this nickname; the vain ruler in Andersen's tale walks out unclothed.

clue.text: Hail fellow? Well, met in short!

definitions.text: Hail fellow? Well, met in short!

parts.words: Hail fellow? Well, met in short!
parts.note: plays on the greeting hail-fellow-well-met: a fellow who deals with hail is a Met man, Met being short for meteorological

explanation.surface: A jovial greeting, hail-fellow-well-met, is broken up and abbreviated.
explanation.walkthrough: The Met Office is Britain's national weather service.
explanation.definitionFit: A forecaster reports on hail and other conditions, and works for the meteorological office.

clue.text: Divers caught in sargasso mesh

indicators.note: caught in means the letters sit trapped inside the run of these clue words

explanation.surface: Scuba divers get tangled in the seaweed nets of the Sargasso Sea.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Divers' reads as swimmers; it is the old adjective meaning several or sundry.
explanation.definitionFit: Divers is an archaic word for several or various, an unspecified number.

clue.text: Walrus left with a mouthful

parts.note: morse is an old word for a walrus

explanation.surface: A walrus is left with food in its mouth.
explanation.definitionFit: A small bite of food, such as a scrap or titbit.

clue.text: In a headlong rush from a grenade explosion

indicators.note: an explosion blows things apart, so these letters are scattered and reassembled

explanation.surface: People flee in a hurry from an exploding grenade.
explanation.walkthrough: The word comes from the Gadarene swine of the Gospels, which rushed down a slope into the sea.
explanation.definitionFit: Biblical swine at Gadara stampeded into the sea, so the adjective describes a reckless, headlong dash.

clue.text: Objects to extremes

explanation.surface: Someone protests about going too far.
explanation.definitionFit: Aims or goals are objects; the farthest points are extremes.

clue.text: Get ready for the night

parts.note: suggests preparing for bed, but means practising for the opening night of a play

explanation.surface: Someone prepares for bedtime.
explanation.definitionFit: Actors run through a play before opening night to prepare it.

clue.text: A panel on the aircraft

parts.note: a board is a flat panel

explanation.surface: A display panel is fitted on a plane.
explanation.definitionFit: Being on a ship, train or plane means being on board it.

clue.text: Blatantly conniving to admit US missile

indicators.note: to admit means the conniving word lets the missile in

parts.note: conniving means sly, cunning
Trident is a submarine-launched missile built in the US

explanation.surface: Someone openly schemes to let an American missile in.
explanation.definitionFit: Doing something loudly and harshly, with no attempt at subtlety, is doing it blatantly.
